newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms at close on U.S. long bond, Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms at close on U.S. long bond, Dow.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed stronger on Friday, buoyed by foreign and local investors stepping into the Mexican financial markets as U.S. long bond yields stabilized and New York stocks rallied, traders said.
"The peso firmed up in a market that closely followed U.S. long bond yields and developments in the Dow Jones," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour closed 3.6 and 2.8 centavos firmer, at 7.8600/7.8630 and 7.8530/7.8580 per dollar.

The Dow Jones was ahead 1.11 percent to 6,516.77 points during late trade in the Mexican foreign exchange market, while yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds stood at 6.74 percent, unchanged from late trade on Thursday.
"There are dollars to invest in Mexico in the international market, and there may be for the coming days," a trader said.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 4.1 centavos firmer at 7.8450/7.8480 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso closed the week 1.5 centavos firmer, but dealers were cautious on its short-term strength due to expected high inflation figures for December.
"Inflation will definitely hit the peso as the figures are expected to be high," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico is due to release inflation data for December next Thursday. Dealers said they expected consumer inflation to be around 3.6 percent.
A Reuters survey of financial professionals MXAAP showed an average forecast of 2.96 percent inflation for December.
